themes: Raws slipped below 18 cents on 18 Nov after USDA's biennial outlook and a weak real; producer hedging stays light, but speculative length is still large, so the band's floor is being tested rather than defended.

Czarnikow's Brazil revision is a shift in timing, not lost cane: rain stoppages push cane into 2027/28, tightening the old-crop balance into March while enlarging next season's start, which argues for a firmer March/May but a heavier deferred curve.
Whites remain the firmer leg on weak EU beet output, and the US domestic market keeps tightening after USDA's beet and cane cuts, walled off from the world price.
Ethanol is a cap rather than a floor: sugar still pays well above hydrous parity, and cheaper US ethanol into Brazil's North/Northeast in the inter-harvest limits support.

items.title: Brazil Weather Widens the Near-Term Deficit
items.takeaway: Czarnikow cut its Centre-South and US crops and widened its 2026/27 world deficit, but frames the Brazil change as timing: rain-stopped cane stays in the field and lifts next season's start, so the 2027/28 crop was raised and the old-crop drawdown is cushioned by earlier surpluses.

items.title: Daily Market Price Updates and Commentary 17th November 2026
items.takeaway: Raws edged up but stayed in the 18c area; consumers would not chase strength and Brazilian growers priced only lightly with the real weak, so trade flow on both sides was thin.

items.title: US Sugar Production Cuts Keep Domestic Prices Supported
items.takeaway: USDA's November cuts to both US beet and cane output (pests hit Louisiana and Florida cane) tighten the US domestic balance despite higher imports; users are holding off at high domestic prices, but sellers are not under pressure.

items.title: Futures and Market Data: 17th November 2026
items.takeaway: Speculators trimmed their net long mostly by selling longs while producers lifted hedges; raws stayed in a narrow range near 18c and the March/May roll is under way, with no strong directional call.

items.title: Understanding Sugar Production
items.takeaway: Explainer on cane versus beet: cane is tropical, ratooned and milled to raws with bagasse as fuel; beet is temperate, harvested in autumn and processed straight to whites.

items.title: Daily Market Price Updates and Commentary 16th November 2026
items.takeaway: Raws stayed in their 18-18.5c band but closed toward the bottom as the real weakened; London March held just above its recent low, leaving a retest open.

items.title: Daily Market Price Updates and Commentary 13th November 2026
items.takeaway: Raws and whites both firmed into the week's close on small-trader buying; London December expired with a sizeable tender talked, and the white premium held near its recent highs.

items.title: Daily Market Price Updates and Commentary 12th November 2026
items.takeaway: Both contracts dipped intraday and settled lower as speculators stayed sidelined after repeated whipsaws; the December white spread eased as open interest ran down ahead of expiry.

items.title: CS Brazil: Sugar or Ethanol? 11th November 2026
items.takeaway: Weekly chart-only tracker of Centre-South mill sugar-versus-ethanol pay; no readable commentary on the free page.
